title: Starbucks to Close 250 Stores in North America
paragraphs: Starbucks plans to close 250 stores across North America as it continues to reshape its business under CEO Brian Niccol.
The company announced the closures on September 24 but did not say which locations would be affected or how many are in the US. The stores represent about 1% of its North American locations.

In a letter to employees, Chief Operating Officer Mike Grams said the stores either were not performing well enough financially or could not provide the experience Starbucks wants for customers and staff.
This is the second major round of closures since Niccol took over in 2024. Last September, Starbucks closed 627 stores in North America and Europe.
At the same time, the company has been updating other coffeehouses to make them feel more comfortable and welcoming.

Changes include softer seating, plants and artwork inspired by the local area. Starbucks has also brought back ceramic cups for customers who want to stay and drink their coffee in the store. More than 1,000 locations in the US and Canada have already been updated, and the company aims to reach 1,500 by September 30.
Grams said the work has helped Starbucks see more clearly which locations are doing well, though some continue to struggle despite employees' efforts.

Starbucks plans to offer affected employees positions at other stores where possible, and severance support when a transfer is not available. Starbucks Workers United, a union representing employees at about 700 US stores, said 20 unionized locations are among those set to close. It has requested more information from Starbucks and said it will negotiate over the closures at those stores.
Starbucks expects the latest closures to cost around $300 million, largely because of lease exits, employee benefits and the loss of store assets.
